project: P3: Do SAE Edits Change What They Claim?
frozen_note: Hypotheses, metrics, units, budget and stop conditions below were written before the first execution on the reported seeds. Any later change must bump config_id and be logged in STATUS.md.

scope.what_this_run_is: CPU-only synthetic toy: implementation checks of edit mismatch, least-norm correction, feasibility, ReLU/JumpReLU/TopK active-set behaviour, norm budget, and rescaling-vs-interference separation.
scope.what_this_run_is_not: No language model, no public SAE, no behavioural evaluation. Nothing here tests the main scientific hypothesis H_MAIN; toy outcomes are mostly fixed by linear algebra and serve as code verification and as a map of failure modes.
scope.H_MAIN: For public LM SAEs, the gap between intended and SAE-re-encoded feature change of a decoder edit predicts external steering failure on held-out prompts, and a local target/protected correction reduces that failure beyond norm-matched rescaling at equal or lower quality loss.

budget.note: Pure-Python stdlib implementation (numpy/torch are not installed and installation is not approved), so execution is single-threaded. If the wall clock is exceeded, remaining experiments are recorded as NOT_RUN (TIMEOUT), never as PASS.

seeds.independent_unit: toy instance = one random draw of (decoder, encoder, bias) for a regime. Base points and target features inside one instance are NOT independent; they are averaged within an instance first.
seeds.dev_seed_note: Used only while writing and debugging code. Not reported.

T2_T5_linear_regimes.alpha_note: Encoder is linear, so every quantity scales linearly in alpha; one alpha suffices.

checks: full_rank_least_norm: random M (k x d, k<=d) -> residual ~0, solution in row space, Pythagorean minimality against null-space perturbations, CGLS == dense within 1e-6 relative
rank_deficient_infeasible: k>d or random target outside range(M) -> residual>0, Fredholm certificate r=t-M x* satisfies M^T r ~ 0 and r.t = ||r||^2 > 0
low_rank_rows: k<=d rows of rank r<k, random target -> infeasible with certificate
rank_deficient_feasible_control: t in range(M) with k>d -> residual ~0
duplicate_rows_conflict: two identical encoder rows with targets (+alpha, 0) -> infeasible for every d, residual = alpha/sqrt(2)
range_infeasible_jumprelu: requested post-activation in (0, theta] is unattainable
topk_eviction: activating an inactive target under TopK with exactly k positive active features must deactivate at least one other feature

T4_activeset_norm.encoder_beta_note: E = (1-beta) D^T + beta D^+, rows rescaled by log-uniform factors in scale_range: an encoder that is neither tied nor biorthogonal.
T4_activeset_norm.protect_rule: P = features active at the base point, excluding the target

TX_external_proxy.description: Synthetic ground-truth dictionary A defines an external readout z_true(x) = A^+ x. The SAE (D, E) is a noisy estimate of (A, A^+). Tests whether internal (SAE-encoder) consistency transfers to the external readout. This is a constructed proxy, NOT a behavioural evaluation.

verification_hypotheses.note: V1-V5 and V7 are mathematical identities; failing any of them means an implementation bug, not a finding. V6 and V8 are descriptive checks whose outcomes are reported as observed.
verification_hypotheses.V1: R0 (E = D^+, m<=d): decoder edit has target_rel_err and leak_rel_all <= identity_tol, and jacobian_ln equals the decoder edit within identity_tol (relative).
verification_hypotheses.V2: R1 (orthonormal D, E = diag(s) D^T): decoder_rescaled has target_rel_err and leak_rel_all <= identity_tol and equals jacobian_ln within identity_tol.
verification_hypotheses.V3: R2 (tied, equiangular coherence c): decoder leak_rel_all = c*sqrt(m-1) within identity_tol; decoder_rescaled leaves the same leakage; jacobian_ln leakage <= identity_tol with norm_ratio = sqrt((G^-1)_jj) > 1.
verification_hypotheses.V4: R4a (m>d, protect all): target+protected system is infeasible (residual_rel > 1e-6) with a valid Fredholm certificate; R4b/R5 (|S u P| <= d): residual_rel <= identity_tol.
verification_hypotheses.V5: jacobian_ln_cgls (JVP/VJP only) matches dense jacobian_ln within 1e-6 relative in every linear regime.
verification_hypotheses.V6: ReLU: whenever no pre-activation changes sign along the segment, the local linear prediction is exact (<= identity_tol). Crossing rates vs alpha, and whether repair converges, are reported as observed.
verification_hypotheses.V7: Trust region: ||delta|| <= tau*(1+1e-9); if ||delta_ln|| <= tau the solution equals delta_ln.
verification_hypotheses.V8: External proxy: report whether jacobian_ln's internal improvement over decoder transfers to the external readout in each case. Expected by construction: transfers when the encoder is accurate, reverses when only the decoder is accurate.

stop_conditions.implementation: If any of V1-V5, V7 fails, stop, fix the code, and do not interpret any toy number.
stop_conditions.project_level: In the later real evaluation: if the correction only improves the internal SAE-encoder metric, or is not distinguishable from norm-matched decoder rescaling on held-out external behaviour and quality, stop claiming a new steering method.
stop_conditions.toy_level: If in every toy regime the achieved mismatch is fully removed by decoder_rescaled (no residual interference), the correction has no toy-level reason to exist; record that and stop.

changelog: v1: initial pre-registration (hypotheses V1-V8, metrics, units, budget, stop conditions).

v1->v2 (after dev seeds 0-2 only, before any report-seed run): T3 CGLS tolerance made explicit (1e-6); low_rank_rows check added; T4b exploratory sparsity axis added because dev inspection showed the v1 T4 ReLU regime has 6-18 active features for d=16 (|S u P|/d = 0.4-1.1), far denser than public LM SAEs. v1 sections are unchanged and remain the primary pre-registered T4 result.
